findings.reason: §16 should state whether it extends the strand-release owner (a bounded write-side release) or is superseded by it, rather than adding a third pointer-lifecycle rule.
findings.text: §16 proposes that a plan-review dispatch refused at admission "remove the pointer on refusal", but does not cite the strand-release mechanism that already releases exactly this pointer class: `_stranded_launch` (`reckon/crew/recovery.py:6600`) and `_discard_stranded_review` (`reckon/crew/recovery.py:1329`), landed at `29e85041d` on 2026-10-03, before this section was written. The §16 symptom run (`r-20261004T213154691561-plan-review-of-a-live-worker-can-be-reached`: pointer at phase `starting`, no `attempt.json`, no supervisor, no pid) is the same pre-spawn-no-evidence shape `_stranded_launch` already recognises, and the plan-review branch of `dispatch_review_for_run` already calls it (`reckon/crew/recovery.py:2389`). Two release paths that disagree on what a pre-spawn pointer means is the defect the section exists to remove.

findings.reason: §3 should name the supervisor's own module so its interface is the spec and the three run-directory records, not a dozen dispatch-private helpers in a file with a known backlog.
findings.text: the per-run supervisor hides substantial behaviour (boundary snapshot, detached spawn, worker wait, signal handling, exit record), but the design gives it no module boundary: the body is `_supervisor_command` inside `dispatch.py` (12,638 lines), reachable only through `supervisor_main.py`, and surrounded by `_supervisor_spec` (:9516), `_supervisor_argv` (:9577), `_start_supervisor` (:9807), `_spawn_detached_supervisor` (:9843), `_spawn_through_fleet` (:9728), `_confirm_supervisor_survived` (:9476) and `_write_boundary_tree_snapshot` (:10053) — plus a second supervisor in `fleet_supervisor.py`. The complexity is real and the interface (the spec in, the run-directory records out) would be smaller than what it hides, but it is never packaged as one.

findings.reason: §10 should resolve the record through `fleet_supervisor.state_directory` rather than forking the path resolver, or the fleet delegation silently falls back to a fork on any host that sets the override.
findings.text: `_fleet_record_path` re-derives the fleet record path from `RECKON_FLEET_RECORD` or `XDG_STATE_HOME/.local/state/fleet/record.json`, but the owner, `state_directory` (`reckon/crew/fleet_supervisor.py:253`), resolves it from `FLEET_STATE_DIR` (default `~/.local/state/fleet`), and `fleet_node.py:306` reads the record through that owner. A batch step started with `FLEET_STATE_DIR` set — the override the supervisor documents and `fleet_supervisor` tests use — publishes its record there, so dispatch reads the default path, finds no record, and forks a supervisor the session step then reaps. That is the exact failure §10 exists to remove, and the plan's §10 "reckon half" adds this second resolver without naming the owner.

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — the per-run supervisor's substantial behaviour is spread across `supervisor_main.py` and ~9 dispatch-private helpers with no module boundary.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — `dispatch._fleet_record_path` forks the fleet-record path resolver already owned by `fleet_supervisor.state_directory`.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §16 adds admission-time release of a plan-review launch pointer without citing the strand-release owner that already releases that pointer class.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the one thin layer, `supervisor_main.py`, states why the launch cannot extend dispatch's entry point (dispatch is already imported, so running it as `-m` re-executes it and opens stderr with runpy's warning).
